notes.title: Announcing Animal Well: Design Works 🐇
notes.content:
In honor of the one year anniversary of ANIMAL WELL's launch, we are extremely excited to announce a new collaboration with Lost In Cult. Please enjoy the official press release below: 


[previewyoutube=Vdq_iG1DIqM;full][/previewyoutube][b]To be enjoyed long after the world loses its internet connection.[/b]

[url=https://www.lostincult.co.uk/animalwell]Lost In Cult x Billy Basso x Bigmode proudly present [b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b].[/url]

Unearth the creation story of one of the decade's most ingenious indies. Developed over a seven year period by its remarkably talented creator Billy Basso, this is a development story for the ages, and one that deserves to be detailed, documented and discussed for years to come.

From forgotten prototypes and years of solo development, to awards and critical acclaim, [b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b] chronicles the incredible journey of this beloved puzzler over 200+ pages.

Crafted alongside Billy Basso, Dan Adelman, and the Bigmode team, [b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b] dives deep into what makes this title so special. Through screenshots of various game builds, developer insight and in-depth analysis, we chart the rise of one of the finest indie games around.

Reflecting on the project, developer Billy Basso said “Lost in Cult has assembled a beautiful collection and the definitive record of Animal Well’s development. This is something I would have wanted for any game I’ve ever loved.”

Alongside our premium Design Works book, we have crafted a series of Deluxe Edition extras to draw you further into the well. From a UV reactive hardcover to a Famicom-inspired pin badge box, we have designed a series of extras to compliment our chronicle of Animal Well.

[b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b] is available to [b]pre-order now[/b]. Our [b]Deluxe Edition is campaign exclusive[/b], and is [b]only available until our campaign ends on 1 July 2025[/b].

[b]Also announcing[/b]: in its physical debut, Billy Basso’s mesmeric Animal Well soundtrack arrives on vinyl! More information below.


[url=https://www.lostincult.co.uk/animalwell][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/84a9b1e4faa8fc20532bdd89b8ae99f72ee14cb8.jpg[/img][/url]

[h2]Standard Edition[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/ffb7482eb76426ff8a2d68d9a7bfec69984ee6ab.jpg[/img]
Crafted alongside the game’s creators, our official [b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b] book documents the development of the title that spawned its own collective puzzle-solving movement.

Uncover never-before-seen prototypes and development screenshots, all accompanied by insight from developer Billy Basso, marketing and business extraordinaire Dan Adelman, and YouTube legend Dunkey’s publisher Bigmode, we showcase how Animal Well came to be.

In keeping with the title’s air of mystery, its cover glows in the dark, highlighting key elements of the cover illustration by Drew Wise.

Designed with signature Lost In Cult flair and attention to detail, this 200+ page section-sewn premium artbook is an essential for those spelunking into the depths of the well.


[h2]Deluxe Edition[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/b1c80255dbe1295e76b20a083f22d87a4ba77390.jpg[/img]
For the Animal Well completionists, we have created the ultimate tribute to Basso’s modern classic. Complimenting the glow-in-the-dark artbook is a range of bespoke Animal Well-themed ephemera celebrating the title’s unique design.

Keep your copy of [b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b] safe with a light-reactive slipcase. Portraying the player character front and centre, this sleek cover is more than meets the eye. Why not see what it looks like under different lighting?

Read your copy to the tranquil sounds of the well with our exclusive looping Animal Well cassette. Featuring a short excerpt from Billy Basso’s etherial soundtrack, this unique tape will loop infinitely, providing hours of aural bliss to your reading experience.

Adorn your walls with exclusive Animal Well art prints from the minds of illustrators Drew Wise, Austin James and madebyabra, each depicting the terrifying, disc-loving dog (yes, dog) in every artist’s unique style.

Inspired by Billy Basso’s childhood Famicom titles, decorate your desk with a mini Animal Well Famicom-style box. Open to reveal four glow-in-the-dark pin badges depicting characters from your journey down the well. Including the dog.

Heavy eyes from reading? Save your progress with our UI-inspired Animal Well bookmark, exclusive to the Deluxe Edition.

[b]Animal Well: Design Works[/b] Deluxe Edition comes packaged in a bespoke presentation and mailing box, ensuring your products reach you in pristine condition. Be sure to hold onto the box to keep your collection safe!

For the [b]first 48 hours[/b], a very special [b]Signed Deluxe Edition[/b] will be available, signed by Billy Basso himself.

[b]The campaign-exclusive Deluxe Edition is only available until 1 July 2025.[/b]


[h2]Animal Well Original Soundtrack Vinyl[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/52e06712d2e25276081dbca946ff0fd138116550.jpg[/img]
In its physical debut, we are proud to bring Billy Basso’s mesmeric score for Animal Well to vinyl in its entirety.

On side A, enjoy Animal Well’s OST unabridged, allowing you to enjoy every whooshing synth from your journey. In addition, experience previously-unreleased tracks that didn't make it to the final game.

Bring the atmosphere of the well to you with side B, containing extended ambient versions of Animal Well’s most iconic numbers.

The vinyl comes with beautiful artwork created by Drew Wise, and features both parallel and locked grooves.

This exclusive transparent [b]Animal Well Original Soundtrack Vinyl[/b] is available standalone and bundled with either edition of Animal Well: Design Works – and is [b]limited to 500 units[/b].

[h2][b][url=https://www.lostincult.co.uk/animalwell]Pre-order here![/url][/b][/h2]

notes.title: Day of the Devs Puzzle Solutions and Some Thoughts
notes.content:
They say never to challenge the Internet since you’ll always lose. I like to think that by challenging the Internet at Day of the Devs, we all won. For anyone reading this who has no idea what I’m talking about, please check out [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/813230/announcements/detail/3361387385185780274]this blog post[/url] post about some secrets I embedded in my Day of the Devs video. If you’re interested in taking a crack at it, please read no further as there be spoilers below.

I am shamelessly and lazily borrowing liberally (i.e., plagiarizing) the solutions write-up written by Discord user @Gami#0826 who pulled all of the puzzles together and credited each person who came up with key components to the solution as well as the exact timing of when each piece was solved. Thank you so much Gami#0826 for crediting everyone for their contribution to the solution!

Before I get into the actual solutions, I want to take a moment to say that whenever you put a piece of creative work out in the world, you always wonder if anyone will notice or care. I can’t put into words how exciting it was to watch the Animal Well Discord community absolutely devour these puzzles. I resisted the temptation to jump in and nudge people in the right direction to the solution (or steer them away from false leads) but only barely.

Here are the solutions after which I have some reflections on the experience below.
[h3]Puzzle 1: Vigenere ciphertext with key[/h3][i]Solved in about 1 hour[/i]
In the background of my video, I included a URL which was intended to be an obvious starting point: [url=http://animalwell.net/fountain]animalwell.net/fountain[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/073fef84fe0a800170843c6662eb28f3c1795d14.png[/img]

Anyone who visited that site was presented with some encrypted text: amtmc xumuacm fcze mtnd ysi wehlnd vtgowqkw oqsaa diqgewa hhrpsi cq pf pftqd uh gijdugr

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/0cfed80a5755d51d40890465977f405cb05b04a7.png[/img]

I wanted to give people a real challenge so rather than have each letter represent another letter in the alphabet, I used an encryption technique created in the 1500s. But how could I expect anyone to realize what encryption mechanism I was using? Well, I made sure to put its creator’s picture in the background!

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qVn2YGvIv0w][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/3f1c4036b1da1eca17c34ecd7a6d1d13bbd8ae4c.png[/img][/url]
Blaise de Vigenère (1523–1596) obviously

Anyone familiar with the Vigenere cipher knows that you need a key to decrypt it. At 0:48 in the video, I included that hint. (Saint Alecz#5555 first in our Discord community to post an image with the waterfall key, and Wormy#0172 was the first to connect the dots. TheHenryGuy#1522 was the first to post an image with the cipher solution.)

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_mDxcDjg9P4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/dd97226f336de8988321b30e059769fd6ffbbf31.png[/img][/url]

There are probably many tools online for decrypting Vigenere ciphers, but I, along with most people, used https://www.dcode.fr/vigenere-cipher:

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iB7E1D_3Na4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/592d79afc4273d69ec0cf29f92bcdc1bf4749d3a.png[/img][/url]

The resulting decrypted text reads:
[i]email subject blue bird for reward cppjwfza oxojv dxfkedw qcrehm cx lo kfifh uo credjvv[/i]

“Email subject blue bird for reward” makes sense, but what about all of that cppjwfza oxojv dxfkedw qcrehm cx lo kfifh uo credjvv nonsense? That suggests a second puzzle!

[h3]Puzzle 2: Vigenere ciphertext without key[/h3]
The challenge of the first puzzle was in figuring out that the text was encrypted with a Vigenere cipher. For the next step, the challenge would be to figure out the key for the remaining text.

The email subject line blue bird was intended as a hint to look closely at the blue bird at 1:38 in the Day of the Devs video. (X3SUCKS#4528 seems to have been the first person in the server to post/directly reference the blue bird in the trailer.)

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_r2K3vvbQ0][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/cbcc962318311faad5034c01847b25665fa2c8db.png[/img][/url]

I also included another hint in the background of the Day of the Devs video: a picture of the Picross DS. (LOLGuy213#7361 was the first to point out this connection.) GizmoArts#7188 then converted the image to the correct Picross nonogram format, and theEggfather#6076 made the nonogram image used below.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/1f341d9941f839063c28ec261d2705f125a8e6de.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/1f84a5b407398f232dfa0ed7c58ed8d4d727033d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/d14fd9e61305ff20ec4bab95ff3f8917c15d23d1.png[/img]

(SuperALA1217#9189 seems to have been the first to post/point out the 1->A 2->B pattern in the video at 0:48.)

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tz_NxOF7RB4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/09f60798e43fc657469f85985516fbef83d270e5.png[/img][/url]

The final step was to pull all of this together by first writing down all of the numbers in the columns and then all of the numbers in the rows and converting them to letters:

1 2 3 4 6 6 7 9 11 12 15 2 11 12 4 5 2 1 2 4 2 3 7 5 6 9 10 10 11 11 11 3 6 2 5 2 1 1 1 1 thus became ABCDFFGIKLOBKLDEBABDBCGEFIJJKKKCFBEBAAAA.

Using this key, one could finally decrypt the remaining text which read: congrats email subject palace to be added to credits. (Congrats to Bardiel#0243 for figuring this out!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/592d79afc4273d69ec0cf29f92bcdc1bf4749d3a.png[/img]

Credit Section: Though there were a few people who came up with the solution at key steps, many others were equally pivotal along the way. Gami#0826 did a wonderful job in identifying these key moments that helped the community move forward, rule out things, and just keep us on track.
[list][*]HomemadeToast#0374 - He made a whole program! We were following some matrix leads on the nonagram part, and he wrote a program to help us convert stuff![/*][*](Red) Mr.Redstone54#7069 - Generally a prominent person during the solving, active as we all helped each other move along during the solve.[/*][*]superALA1217#9189 - first found the column number to letter conversion hint, and kept posting it until someone actually followed it finally.[/*][*]Minoin#1775/BurningSpade#5989 - Both helped with the ‘fish’ lead at different times, Minion bringing it up first. Although it led to nothing, it helped us weed out stuff that wasn’t directly part of this puzzle!’[/*][*]And many many many more, sorry if I didn’t specifically mention some of you all, I had a hard time deciding who to credit or not to list directly.[/*][/list]

[h3]Puzzle 3: Inspect Element[/h3]
Although this puzzle wasn’t created specifically for Day of the Devs, the act of throwing down the gauntlet to the Internet caused people to explore every nook and cranny and ultimately discover this. About 3 months ago, I included on the Animal Well website a little note to email me with the subject line DARK FOREST. The only way to notice this was to go to the website, inspect elements, and scroll to the bottom of the elements tab:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41935629/fa6a77d971f171db53f1cd5de18bf4ea92b063f5.png[/img]

To any naysayers out there who feel that it will be impossible for me to create puzzles that will take literally years for people to solve, I will just point out that this one was just sitting around for people to discover for months. Who knows what other puzzles may be lying dormant, just waiting for the right person to happen upon it?

[h2]Reflections[/h2]
[h3]1 - The beginnings of a real community[/h3]
The word “community” is often tossed around like so many other marketing buzzwords. Discord is often seen as the place for communities to come together, but aside from a common interest in a certain game, a lot of Discord servers lack what really makes a community: people getting to know each other; people coming together for a common purpose; people actually enjoying one another’s company. As I watched the Discord server spring to life, I felt like I was seeing an actual community form in real time. Everyone was respectful of each other’s ideas and contributions, and everyone was having fun tackling the challenge together. It was as if I had inadvertently created something larger than a game, and I thank everyone on the Discord server for coming together the way they did.

[h3]2 - With great power comes great responsibility[/h3]
When I put out the Day of the Devs video, I focused on the clues I was deliberately including but didn’t put enough thought into what people might mistake for clues. Watching the Discord community tear through the puzzles was like watching a feeding frenzy, and when people were on the right track it was shocking how fast people locked onto the solution. But when people started to fixate on a red herring, it was hard not to feel a little bad.

I want to continue putting out challenges to the community, but at the same time, I realize that I’m going to need to be more cognizant of what people might accidentally assume is a clue but isn’t. I’ll be honest that I haven’t figured out the right way to do this yet. I could jump in and tell people if they’re on the wrong track, but that seems too heavy handed. Likewise, a lack of any response from me could be misconstrued as tacit acknowledgement that there is a clue to be found. When puzzles could be anywhere, they could be everywhere. I want to make sure solving these challenges is fun and rewarding, not a series of frustrating dead ends.

[h3]3 - This is going to be a regular thing from now on[/h3]Notwithstanding my concerns of having people over-analyze every little thing I put out there, this was just too much fun to be a one-off. When I put together the Day of the Devs video I explicitly told everyone that there was a puzzle in it. From now on, there will be no such explicit notice. Puzzles may be lurking anywhere and everywhere. The gauntlet has been thrown.
